criteria.name: Thumb-stop cover
criteria.notes: Unchanged and still strong. The hook is a named tension in 11 words plus UPDATE, set in huge serif that reads at the 432 px thumb. The PBR reversed brass STRATEGIC PARTNER is the deck's best object and is the filing's own phrase. Two things hold it below 9. 'AEA' is never expanded on the cover. And the four-line headline and the brass line compete as two focal points. Nothing on the cover reads as Alaskan apart from the words 'Cook Inlet'.

criteria.name: Story arc & swipe momentum
criteria.notes: The craft cycle didn't touch the arc. 01 to 02, 06 to 07 and 08 to 09 land. The flow critic's weak junctions (02 to 03, 03 to 04, 04 to 05, 05 to 06) remain, with no text plants. 03 is still the third dense frame in a row before the 04 turn, and it is still the predicted bail point. The D5 tease still doesn't complete: 03 cuts the mirrored C of STRATEGIC at mid frame, while 04 brings in the whole STRATEGIC at y 0.88 under the motion's foot. 03 and 05 could be reordered with little loss.

criteria.name: Artwork craft & genuine detail
criteria.notes: Up from 6.5. Most of the gain is removing the 03 defect. 03's ghost glyphs are gone and every brass line lands whole, but the forme is still flat CG. The seven slabs are uniform ochre, and the glyphs carry a default bevel emboss. The oak is near-flat tan, the chase a flat grey frame, and the quoins still read as three grey boxes with dots. The proud line drops no visible cast onto 66 HIVES. 06's slugs now carry reversed names (AEA, ORPC, CIRI, KENAITZE) that read at full size and blur at thumb. The galley floor is still one bright rectangle of uniform static, the brightest and largest object on the breather, so it reads as TV snow, not a graded mezzotint. 08 has its full name and the pool is clear of the fixture. Its seven lead slugs are still white wireframe outlines that cast nothing under the key, the only white-line-on-black frame in a rendered deck. 09 is improved: the sheet has a key falloff, and the housing reads as dark painted steel with lit bevels. It still reads as a product mock: the ink pad is a flat, saturated plastic-blue slab with no felt, and the sheet is a clean card. 07's sheet is trimmed with no blank foot, but it is still a near-flat card with a soft drop shadow. The chart on it is excellent information design. Strengths hold: 01 is genuinely rendered (PBR brass, brushed steel, a lit pool), and 05's copper DEM plate is real engraving. The deck is strong in places, but four frames still lean on defaults or flat regions, so 7.0, not higher.

criteria.name: Story-art fusion
criteria.notes: The art encodes the story. The reversed STRATEGIC PARTNER is the filing's phrase, and the forme sets the ask's numbers in metal. 05 has the four filed corners and a 3.5-mile cable on the real Upper Cook Inlet DEM. 07 is a 134-mark census with 3 gold DeepGreen marks. 08 has 7 slugs for the motions plus 2 gold for the silent names. 09's wheels read 11 02. 06's slugs now carry the application's four names, which restores the motif. A stranger would guess 'a filing and who answered it' more readily than 'a Cook Inlet data center'.

criteria.name: Alaska authenticity & local relevance
criteria.notes: Named throughout: AEA, CIPLink, Curtis W. Thayer, the Peninsula Clarion, Nikiski, East and West Foreland, CIRI, the Kenaitze Indian Tribe, the Kenai Peninsula Borough, the City of Kenai, Rebecca Long of Talkeetna, GCI, and now the Alaska Commercial Fisheries Conservation Alliance by its full name. 05's geography sits on the real DEM, with the box in the narrows. The honesty guards hold. The one imported beat is that the letterpress world carries no Alaskan material.

criteria.name: Insight density & factual weight
criteria.notes: Every content slide adds a new verified primary specific. The deck has two verbatim replies, the permit's legal effect, said against filed, 'substantially smaller' with no new size, the 134 and 117 census with its 59 and 58 split, and six movants in filing order with positions. 06 is thin by design. On 07, '59 BY SEPTEMBER 25TH  58 SINCE' still doesn't say it counts public comments rather than all 134 filings.

The oak is near-flat tan and the chase a flat grey frame. The three quoins are grey boxes with dots. The proud STRATEGIC PARTNER line stands no visibly higher than its neighbours and casts nothing.

Give the proud line a hard contact plus a soft cast down and to the left onto 66 HIVES and TURBINES. Add cavity shade in the lead spacing, warped figure in the oak, and wedge-shaped quoins with a lit upper-right face.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The galley floor, the largest and brightest object on the breather, is one rectangle of uniform white-noise static at a single value. It reads as TV snow, not a mezzotint. The slug names read at full size but are mush at thumb.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Threshold the floor dots against a graded tone study: brightest at the far lip beside the slugs, falling smoothly to near black at the near end, with a scraped lit far lip, a lee near wall and a contact cast. This also makes 06 the true tonal trough, below 08.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The seven lead slugs are still white wireframe outlines with uniform line weight and no cast under the skylight. It is the only white-line-on-black frame in an otherwise rendered deck.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Ramp each slug's front hatch from dense at the foot (lee) to sparse at the top (lit). Cross-hatch the tops at a lower value. Drop a hatched cast down and to the left from each slug onto the galley floor, so the one-key physics reads.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: It still reads as a product mock, not a still life. The ink pad is a flat, saturated plastic-blue slab with no felt texture or inked centre, and the sheet is a clean card with only a broad gradient.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Give the pad a felt bump and roughness variation with a darker, wetter inked centre and a lit tin rim. Add fibre and a faint printed margin to the sheet, so the lower third carries surface detail.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The docket sheet is trimmed, but it is still a near-flat pale card with a soft drop shadow, and it echoes 02 and 04's proof cards at contact-sheet scale.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Run the sheet through 02's relit paper heightfield with a key falloff from the upper right. Add a lifted lower-left corner with a lit lip and cast, and faint ledger rules so it reads as a clerk's sheet, not a card.

editor_notes_for_email: Score: 8.42 against the round-4 threshold of 7.7, with no hard fails. Artwork scored 7.0 after the craft cycle (6.5 before), still below the 8.5 craft floor, but the one required cycle is done. The 03 ghost-glyph bug is fixed. Facts to know before posting: AEA's motion is dated October 7th (02, 04, caption) and filed October 8th (08, labelled FILED). The 117 public filings come from 115 distinct names, and October 13th's 18 are a weekend and Columbus Day backlog, not a one-day surge. The CIRI and Kenaitze line means only that no filing was listed when the docket was pulled late on October 22nd. ORPC's 'configured to interface with' is ORPC quoting a DeepGreen filing the run didn't read, probably the June 26th supplement. Thayer's 'oppose' is a newspaper quote, not a filing. The deck leaves out DeepGreen's line that it never claimed a formal binding partnership with AEA; expect it in the comments. Visual caveats a careful reader may notice: 06's galley floor reads as static, 08's slugs as wireframe, and 09's ink pad as plastic.
